messages.text: Quick update on tonight's checkout blip for Acme — looks like it was our bad deploy, I've already apologised to Dana and told her we rolled it back.
SCIM for Acme: required. We're building it alongside SSO per their security review.
Update: SCIM for Acme is deferred. Pushing it to Q1 so we don't split focus before the December SSO date — SSO is the harder deadline.
Actually, SCIM for Acme is back in scope for December — InfoSec flagged manual provisioning as a compliance gap in their latest review, so we need it alongside SSO after all.
For the record, SCIM for Acme is deferred to Q1 — that's still what's on our roadmap for this quarter.
For the record on the Acme work: this is SAML-based SSO with Okta, targeting December. SP-initiated flow is in review now.
Started scaffolding the SCIM endpoints for Acme this week too, ahead of the broader rollout.
Kickoff done with Globex. Provisioning the US tenant tomorrow, 50 seats per the handoff notes.
18:10 IST — checkout API 5xx spike, suspect our 18:00 deploy. Rolling back now.
18:40 IST — rolled back, no change in error rate. Now looking at AWS us-east-1 — ELB is showing degraded health checks. This looks like the real root cause, not our deploy.
18:52 IST — recovered. 12% of requests failed between 18:05 and 18:52. Acme and Globex both affected. ~300 writes were queued during the window and are replaying now.
